summary: Design the sim auto-run, mode strips, QC preview selector, MM/KCD simulators and upstream release-check rule; then cross-check

designs.summary: Auto-run is a LibKa0s default with no new public surface. Starting from the verb layer plays the session on its own: a typed or picker `start`, and a typed or button `restart`. The members sim:Start and sim:Restart stay literal, so host suites that script through them are untouched. Arming sets playing at once, building phase included, so Pause works before step 1. The first tick runs through sim:After(0) once ready() has fired, using a listener the timeline registers on itself; Sim.lua does not change. Later ticks wait stepDelay(step). A manual step, typed or a click on the next row, takes over a playing run: it holds the run (no tick, paused) and then acts. A click-ahead does the same. A manual act leaves the run paused, so Resume is always offered. Run all goes and RUN_ALL leaves Sim.STRINGS. The controls become Pause/Resume, Restart and Stop, three equal buttons across the bar. The Resume button sends `resume` when paused and `run` otherwise, so a session started through the member is still playable. `run` stays as the resume synonym. The usage text keeps the substring `start a simulation.` that host suites match. The Sim key moves 2.2.4 to 2.3.5 (SimTimeline 3, SimPanel 5). Host fallout is three items. DropWatcher has the most: the ready line, the step-delay tooltip, about ten typed-start cases in test_sim_scenario/test_sim_panel, and data-flow/schema/settings/smoke docs. BankLedger and LootHistory each have their tooltip, comments, README and docs, and LootHistory also has its panel controls case. WhatGroup only lists the vendored Sim files and PGFE has no simulator, so neither needs an item. No standard section names Run all or the controls. WS-01 adds the one fact that a session started from the verb or panel plays on its own, in preview-mode's simulator paragraph and library-stack's Sim row.

Design: Ka0sAddonsCommonTasks docs/2026-10-23-SIM_PREVIEW_MODE_STRIPS/inputs/design-autorun.md sections 2.1-2.4 (decisions A1-A12). Owner scope A.1 and C.1.

VERSIONS. SimTimeline.lua TIMELINE_MINOR 2 -> 3 (LibKa0s/SimTimeline.lua:65) and SimPanel.lua SIM_PANEL_MINOR 4 -> 5 (LibKa0s/SimPanel.lua:58). Sim.lua stays at 2, so the key goes 2.2.4 -> 2.3.5. If an earlier item on this run's branch has already bumped either file for v1.76.0 (the sim strip may touch SimPanel), do not bump it again: each file bumps once per release (docs/releasing.md step 2). In that case extend that item's version document and CHANGELOG section instead of writing new ones.

TESTS FIRST (red before the code). Add a new suite tests/test_sim_autoplay.lua and register it in tests/run.lua's sim group (line 93-94, after test_sim_verbs). Reuse the bench shape of tests/test_sim_timeline.lua:30-74: a three-step scenario, a sized one, prepare calling ready() at once unless holdReady is set, the kit clock m.__fireTimers()/m.__timers(), and a stand-in Sim.__AttachPanel capturing ctx. Cases:
(1) A typed `start three` with a synchronous ready: Status().playing is true, nothing has played, exactly one live timer with delay 0. One fire plays `a`, and the next pending delay is 2 (or d.stepDelay).
(2) A typed start with ready held: playing is true, the state word is building, and no timer exists. b.readies[1]() leaves one timer of delay 0, and firing it plays `a`.
(3) The member sim:Start{} arms nothing (playing false, no timer), and the member sim:Restart() arms nothing.
(4) A typed `restart` arms the new session: pos 0, playing, one timer of delay 0. No timer of the old session survives.
(5) A refused typed start (unknown scenario, or already running) arms nothing.
(6) Pause while armed and building answers true and sets paused. A later ready() schedules nothing. Resume while still building answers false, "building" and keeps paused true (A11).
(7) A typed `step` while a run plays (after the first fire): the pending tick is cancelled (no live timer), the next step plays at once, then playing is false and paused is true, and a later fire plays nothing.
(8) A typed `step` while armed and building answers building and leaves the run armed: ready() still schedules the tick.
(9) ctx.runTo(3) while a run plays holds it, plays up to step 3 back to back, then leaves playing false and no live timer. With steps still left after the target it leaves paused true.
(10) A second runTo while a first one polls a closed gate retargets rather than answering playing. sim:Run() during a pending RunTo poll still answers playing (C.2 unchanged).
(11) A manual step from the waiting state (member start, ready, then sim:Step()) leaves paused true while steps remain, and finish clears paused.
(12) Typed `run` after a manual step resumes and plays the next step at once.
(13) Stop while armed and building leaves no timer, and a stale ready() from the stopped session schedules nothing.
(14) The USAGE_START and USAGE_RUN lines read exactly as below.
In tests/test_sim_panel.lua, add cases:
(a) Running, the controls are exactly pause, restart and stop (f.controls.run is nil), each CONTROL_W = 116 wide at x 0, 122 and 244.
(b) The picker's Start click leaves the session playing with one pending timer of delay 0, and its printed lines equal the typed `start` lines (the existing typed-equals-clicked case at :431-442 stays).
(c) While playing, clicking the ready row holds the run and plays one step: the button now reads RESUME and the tooltip command is `/host sim resume`.
(d) While playing, clicking a row two ahead plays up to it and the run is held.
(e) After a member start (nothing playing, not paused) the Pause/Resume button reads RESUME, is enabled once ready, sends `run` (its tooltip shows `/host sim run`), and starts play.
(f) Restart's button arms the new session.
(g) Sim.STRINGS.RUN_ALL is nil.

CODE, SimTimeline.lua.
- Add to the run record R (current(), :144) the field awaiting=false.
- Add the file-local helpers hold(T,R), kick(T,R) and arm(T) as written in design-autorun.md 2.2. hold cancels the timer, sets playing=false, paused=true, settling=false, awaiting=false and target=nil, then notifies. kick: if R.awaiting and R.playing and live(T,R) and ctx.ready(), clear awaiting and schedule(T,R,0,tick). arm: R=current(T), set paused=false, playing=true, target=nil and awaiting=true, notify, then kick.
- In lib.__AttachTimeline (:555), register `sim:AddListener(function() kick(T, T.R) end)` so it is the first listener.
- Thread T through the verbs: runVerb(T, line), verbStart(T, words), verbControl(T, verb), verbHost(T, spec, words), and `function sim.RunVerb(_, line) return runVerb(T, line) end`.
- verbStart calls arm(T) after sim:Start answers true. verbControl calls arm(T) after sim:Restart() answers true.
- sim.Step: `local R = current(T); if R and R.playing and not blocked(T, R) then hold(T, R) end; local step, code = stepOnce(T, R, true); if R and live(T, R) and not R.playing and R.pos < #R.steps and T.ctx.ready() then R.paused = true end; return step, code`.
- runTo (:305): replace `if R.playing then return false, "playing" end` with `if R.playing then hold(T, R) end`. In runToPass (:298-301), when it ends live and R.pos < #R.steps, also set R.paused = true.
- Pause (:346): also clear awaiting. Its check `not R.playing` already covers an armed run during building.
- Resume (:355): `local code = blocked(T, R)` first, and if code return false, code; then paused=false; return sim:Run().
- finish (:200): also set paused=false and awaiting=false.
- STRINGS: USAGE_START = "%s start <scenario> [size]: start a simulation. It plays at once; pause it to step by hand." and USAGE_RUN = "%s run: play the remaining steps (the same as resume)."
- Header comment (:1-60): the members block gains the auto-run (the verb layer arms; the members do not), the hold rule and paused-after-a-manual-act. Keep every function at CCN 15 or below; split runVerb's T threading into helpers if needed.

CODE, SimPanel.lua.
- Drop RUN_ALL from STRINGS (:90).
- Add CONTROL_W = floor((ROW_W - 2 * BUTTON_GAP) / 3) beside BUTTON_W (:417).
- buildControls (:712-727): the list is { {"pause","PAUSE"}, {"restart","RESTART"}, {"stop","STOP"} }, each makeButton(c, CONTROL_W, ...) at (i-1) * (CONTROL_W + BUTTON_GAP).
- paintControls (:746-762): left = st.ready and pos < total. If st.playing: __verb "pause", label PAUSE, enabled. Else: label RESUME, __verb = st.paused and "resume" or "run", enabled = left. Restart and Stop stay enabled.
- Header (:24-47): one sentence that a click while the run plays holds it first (the timeline's rule), and that the controls are Pause/Resume, Restart and Stop.

- tests/test_sim_host.lua:227, :275 and :295 (start -> run: either drop the run and fire timers, or assert run answers playing).
- tests/test_sim_session.lua:178.

Write *What changed at this version* (auto-run from the verb layer; members unchanged; hold-on-manual-act; paused after a manual act; Resume's building check; Status().playing true while armed and building; controls Pause/Resume, Restart, Stop with the Resume-sends-run rule; RUN_ALL removed; the two usage lines). Give `Since` SimTimeline 3 / SimPanel 5 to Step, RunVerb start/restart, Pause, Resume and the controls row.

designs.summary:
This makes the library's test strip generic without adding a new library member. LK-10 adds `opts.kind = "sim"` to `W.TestStrip`, which draws a cyan band ({0.35,0.80,1.00} at 0.12, the collection's existing simulation color). It also adds a read-only `strip.kind` field and bumps Widgets to minor 14 (key 14.1.4.3.2). TestStrip and TEST_STRIP stay the only members, and every existing call stays the same.

One header-word rule applies to every window: a mode word in the header shows only while its mode is on and that mode's strip is not on screen. In practice the word goes whenever the strip is visible, and it stays when the window is minimized or when there is no Widgets library. No locale key becomes dead.

Per-addon items:
- **BL-10:** a second, sim-kind strip on the Browser, the TEST MODE badge kept only as the degraded fallback, and the SessionWindow strip switched to kind "sim" (field renamed to simStrip).
- **DW-10:** a new sim banner that carries SimTip, and the TEST MODE / SIMULATION words dropped except when minimized or degraded.
- **LH-10:** a sim strip beside the test strip, with the badge kept only as the degraded fallback.
- **MM-01:** the TEST MODE title word dropped while the strip is shown, and kept when minimized or degraded.

WS-05 writes the rule into the standard: preview-mode, standalone-windows, the library-stack-§7 Widgets row, anti-pattern #97, AUDIT.md, NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT and the v2.87.0 ruling.

Left alone, as the owner asked: QuickComms, AuraMaster, WhatGroup and KickCD header words, MultiMeters' session-line "Test", and BankLedger's step-panel title. The MultiMeters and KickCD sim strips themselves belong to the simulator agents, which build on LK-10.

designs.summary:
MultiMeters /mm sim (MultiMeters#60, OWNER_SCOPE A and B4) is planned as 11 serial M3 items, MM-10 to MM-20. The design note is in inputs/design-mm-sim.md.

**What the code shows today:**
- The meter is already routed through the eight Compat shims, and Provider is their only caller, proved by the scan in tests/test_provider.lua:60-98.
- The world reads are not routed. The unit, group and role reads in Roster.lua:222-298, IsInGroup and IsInInstance in Visibility.lua, the four UnitAffectingCombat call sites, and DrillDown's OpenDeathRecapUI all go straight to _G.
- Events sit in one EVENTS table (core/MultiMeters.lua:125), but there is no single entry function the simulator could deliver through.
- The only SavedVariables a session can reach are db.global.roster (Roster remembered/Forget) and the window segment pins (SetSegment, and the stale-pin repair DropStaleSegment).

**Design:**
- Prerequisites first: Compat members for the world reads (MM-10), and one OnGameEvent/DeliverEvent entry with a real-event filter hook (MM-11).
- The rest follows the BankLedger/LootHistory pattern on LibKa0s-Sim-1.0:
  - MM-12: core/SimSetup.lua right after Compat. Formatters, spell reads and the travel probes are pure. ResetAllCombatSessions, ChatSender (prints [sim]) and OpenDeathRecap are guarded.
  - MM-13: a closed, seeded world. The real player is the local player, the group mates are invented, and session ids start at 1000000. Every meter, recap, unit, group, instance and combat read has a provider, and values are plain numbers.
  - MM-14: drivers that fire the client's events in the client's order. A fight is ticked over time with sim:After, and a gate holds the run while a fight is still going.
  - MM-15: the host. Refusals cover stood down, test mode, combat, instance, group and General visibility set to never. A real-event classifier stops the run on combat, a loading screen, joining a group or entering an instance, and swallows real meter events. Stops also come from stand-down and profile changes. The stop puts the pins back and resyncs through ENTERING_WORLD and METER_SESSION, never through METER_RESET, which would wipe the real remembered roster. While a run is active the roster store is session-only, the stale-pin repair is skipped and test mode is refused.
  - MM-16: the four #60 scenarios and a headless e2e suite. It asserts what the engine produced, that the live meter is never called, that nothing is sent, and that profile and global SavedVariables are byte-identical after a run.
  - MM-17: the LibKa0s sim-flavor strip on every window, with no SIMULATION word in any header.
  - MM-18: a sim.stepDelay slider (1 s default, 0.5 to 10), matching LootHistory and BankLedger.
  - MM-19: a diagnostics sim section.
  - MM-20: docs and the in-repo spec.
- The simulator does not simulate secrets or the Combat restriction. Secret handling stays covered by the existing mock_secrets suites.

items.title: One dispatch entry for game events: NS:OnGameEvent, NS.DeliverEvent and the real-event filter hook
items.spec:
MultiMeters#60 prerequisite ('its events go through one dispatch table') and Sim host contract H3.

FILES: core/MultiMeters.lua (621 lines, target about 690)
- Keep the EVENTS array (:125-195) as the single source.
- Build `NS.HANDLER_BY_EVENT = { [event] = methodName }` from EVENTS at file load, after EVENTS. If an event appears twice, raise at load: one row per event is the dispatch contract.
- OnEnable (:197-218): register every row with the one handler name `"OnGameEvent"`, using `register(self, EVENTS[i][1], "OnGameEvent", rejected)`. Rejection collection is unchanged.
- New `function NS:OnGameEvent(event, ...)`:
  `local f = NS.RealEventFilter; if f and f(event, ...) then return end; NS.DeliverEvent(event, ...)`
  Comment: the filter is the simulator host's hook, set only by modules/Sim.lua while a session runs; it is consulted on the real path only.
- New `function NS.DeliverEvent(event, ...) -> n`: answers 0 when HANDLER_BY_EVENT has no row for event, or when event is listed in NS.State.rejectedEvents (the client never registered it). Otherwise it calls `NS[method](NS, event, ...)` and answers 1. This is exactly what the client's registration would have called, so the simulator passes it as `deliver`.
- The existing handlers keep their signatures `(self, event, ...)` and their perf brackets.
- Add `NS.RealEventFilter = nil` with a doc comment where the other State seams are documented, or in this file's header.

TESTS FIRST (new tests/test_dispatch.lua, declared in tests/run.lua SUITES after test_lifecycle)
- Every EVENTS row is registered with handler 'OnGameEvent'.
- HANDLER_BY_EVENT has exactly one row per event.
- NS:OnGameEvent('GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE') sends MSG.ROSTER_CHANGED.
- DeliverEvent answers 1 for a known event and 0 for an unknown one.
- DeliverEvent answers 0 for an event in State.rejectedEvents and calls nothing.
- A RealEventFilter answering true consumes the event: no message is sent and DeliverEvent is not called. One answering false lets it through.
- DeliverEvent ignores the filter.
- Varargs reach the handler: OnMeterSession gets statType and sessionID, OnEnteringWorld gets isLogin and isReload.

items.title: modules/SimDrivers.lua: drivers that edit the world and fire the client's events, with ticked fights
items.spec:
FILES
- New modules/SimDrivers.lua (about 320 lines), published as `NS.SimHost.Drivers`, TOC after modules\SimWorld.lua. Every event goes through `NS.Sim:Fire(event, ...)`, read at call time. Every timer is `NS.Sim:After` (never C_Timer or AceTimer).
- Drivers (w = NS.SimHost.world):
  - FormGroup(n, raid): World.SetGroup; Fire GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE.
  - Disband(): World.SetGroup(w, 1); Fire GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE.
  - Zone(key): World.SetZone; Fire PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD(false, false), then ZONE_CHANGED_NEW_AREA.
  - Pull(fight): World.OpenSegment(fight.name); w.combat = true; Fire PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED; then Tick.
  - Tick(fight): World.Tick(w, fight.secondsPerTick); run any fight.deaths whose tick == the current tick through World.Die; Fire DAMAGE_METER_CURRENT_SESSION_UPDATED.
  - EndFight(fight): w.combat = false; World.CloseSegment; Fire PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED; then DAMAGE_METER_COMBAT_SESSION_UPDATED(stat.enumValue, segment.sessionID) for each entry of Constants.STATS in order; then DAMAGE_METER_CURRENT_SESSION_UPDATED.
  - Reset(): `NS.Provider.Reset()` (the player's own path, which the guarded ResetAllCombatSessions answers, firing DAMAGE_METER_RESET after 0 s).
  - Fight(fight, session): runs Pull and the first tick now. It then books ticks 2..fight.ticks with `NS.Sim:After(TICK * k, ...)`, TICK = 0.5, and the last booked tick calls EndFight when fight.ends. It increments `w.pending` per booking and decrements it as each runs. Answers a detail line ('%d ticks booked').
- Event order follows the client. Pull and EndFight are documented with the client's order (REGEN before the meter's session event).
- `Drivers.TICK` is exported for tests.

designs.summary:
KickCD gets `/kcd sim` (KickCD#38, OWNER_SCOPE A/B2/B4), built on LibKa0s-Sim-1.0 the way BankLedger and LootHistory are, in ten serial items, all M3.

**Prerequisites (no library dependency):**
- KC-01 closes the compat gaps. Nine direct `_G` unit and cast reads in `State.lua`, `IconGrid.lua`, `IconGrid_Visibility.lua` and `Castbar.lua` move behind new Compat members. `GetCastingInfo` and `GetChannelInfo` are rerouted through those members. A pure `Compat.NewDuration` wraps `C_DurationUtil.CreateDuration`.
- KC-02 builds the one dispatch table KickCD lacks. A route registry is fed by `NS.RegisterEventList` and `Util.NewUnitCastFilter`. `NS.DeliverEvent` replays exactly the handlers the client would run: AceEvent routes still registered (read from CallbackHandler's registry) and armed cast filters for the event's unit.

**The simulator (depends on KC-RV, v1.76.0):**
- KC-03: the seam (`core/SimSetup.lua`, straight after Compat; no guarded members, because KickCD sends and casts nothing), the stubs, the `sim` feature verb and the `confirm`/`info` icons.
- KC-04: the simulated world and its providers. These are cooldowns, GCD, charges, target and focus units, and casts with the interruptible flag, using real client duration objects.
- KC-05: the session host. It covers the descriptor, refusals (stood down, perf, unlocked, combat, instance, group, no grid, no usable spell, no duration support), `prepare`, and a two-phase stop that re-syncs the engine to the real client.
- KC-06: real-world interference and destructive surfaces. Combat, a loading screen, a group join, a profile change and an unlock each stop the session. `resetall` and unlock refuse while it runs. The stand-down stops it first, and diagnostics gets a `sim` section.
- KC-07: state-driven step drivers, so every `[sim]` line is true however the run is paced.
- KC-08: the made-up party and the four #38 scenarios (M+ pull, boss kick rotation with charges, uninterruptible cast and kick on cooldown, member leaving mid-pull), with a headless end-to-end suite per scenario and a saved-data byte-identity check.
- KC-09: the sim strip from the LibKa0s sim flavor (LK-10..19). It is parented to UIParent and placed the way the existing unlock strip is: above the unit label or the target grid, falling back to the focus grid, then to a floating spot. So the visibility mode never hides it while a session runs.
- KC-10: the documentation ripple and the 12 smoke checks (SIM-1..12).

**Key decision.** KickCD tracks only the player's own cooldowns against the target's and focus's casts; it has no party tracking. So #38's party is narrative only (names in `[sim]` lines, kicks ending enemy casts), and each scenario is mapped onto the engine path it stresses. That is the one open question for the owner.

**Other decisions:**
- A fixed 1 s step delay with no slider, because the scenarios tell a timed story.
- No gate, because nothing in KickCD settles asynchronously.
- No CHANGELOG (KickCD has none) and no version bump.

items.title: Compat gaps: unit and cast readers behind NS.Compat, read at call time, plus a pure duration constructor (simulator prerequisite, H1)
items.spec:
WHY. Host contract H1 and compat-§1 (KickCD#38's prerequisite): the seam (KC-03) can only answer the client reads that go through `NS.Compat`, read at call time. Today nine reads bypass it (design-kc-sim §1.1).

TESTS FIRST. New `tests/test_compat_units.lua`, registered in `tests/run.lua`'s suite list. Write it red, then green:
1. Each new member, with the client API mocked present, passes the arguments straight through and returns every value, nil holes included. Each one, with the API absent, answers the documented absent value:
   - `UnitExists`: false
   - `UnitCanAttack`: **true**, which preserves today's `if _G.UnitCanAttack and not ...` semantics
   - `UnitIsDead`: false
   - `UnitCastingInfo` and `UnitChannelInfo`: nil
   - `UnitCastingDuration` and `UnitChannelDuration`: nil
   - `NewDuration`: nil
2. A swap test. Replace `NS.Compat.UnitCastingInfo` (and the channel, duration and `UnitCanAttack` members) with spies, then call `Compat.GetCastingInfo("target")`. The record is built from the spies' answers, which proves `GetCastingInfo` and `GetChannelInfo` read the members at call time.
3. A swap test for each converted call site. With the `NS.Compat.Unit*` members swapped for fakes that report a hostile caster on `target`:
   - `NS.State.IsHostileUnitCasting("target")` answers true;
   - `State.ApplyInterruptibleAlpha` calls `SetAlphaFromBoolean` with the fake's flag;
   - `IconGrid.InstanceCasting({unit = "target"})` answers true;
   - IconGrid_Visibility's interruptible resolve reads position 8 or 7 from the fakes;
   - `Castbar:Reevaluate` starts the bar from the fakes.
   The `_G` APIs are deliberately left answering "nothing", so a test only passes if the call site goes through Compat.
4. `NewDuration`, with a mocked `C_DurationUtil.CreateDuration` whose object records `SetTimeFromStart(start, dur)`, answers that object. A constructor or setter that raises answers nil and does not raise.

IMPLEMENTATION.
- `core/Compat.lua`: add a `-- Unit and cast readers (the simulator's seam answers these; docs/compat-layer.md)` section after the Specialization block:
  - `Compat.UnitExists(unit)`
  - `Compat.UnitCanAttack(unit)`, which reads `_G.UnitCanAttack("player", unit)`; the player is always the first argument at every call site
  - `Compat.UnitIsDead(unit)`
  - `Compat.UnitCastingInfo(unit)` and `Compat.UnitChannelInfo(unit)`, raw multi-return passthroughs
  - `Compat.UnitCastingDuration(unit)` and `Compat.UnitChannelDuration(unit)`
  - `Compat.NewDuration(startTime, duration)`: `local du = _G.C_DurationUtil; if not (du and du.CreateDuration) then return nil end`, then pcall the constructor and pcall `d:SetTimeFromStart(startTime, duration)`, answering nil on any failure. Comment that it is PURE in the simulator's seam (a constructor answers for nobody) and that the setter name is to be confirmed by SM-KC-1.
  - Rewrite `effectiveNotInterruptible` (`:322-327`), `GetCastingInfo` (`:332-344`) and `GetChannelInfo` (`:481-493`) to call `Compat.UnitCanAttack`, `Compat.UnitCastingInfo`, `Compat.UnitCastingDuration` and the channel twins **through the table at call time**, never `_G` and never a captured local.
  - Leave `Compat.DebugInterrupt` reading the raw client, and add a comment saying it dumps the REAL client on purpose.
- `core/State.lua:89-96` (`IsHostileUnitCasting`) and `:116-137` (`ApplyInterruptibleAlpha`): use `NS.Compat.UnitExists`, `NS.Compat.UnitCanAttack`, and `Compat._firstReturn(NS.Compat.UnitCastingInfo, unit)` / `NS.Compat.UnitCastingInfo(unit)` and the channel twins, keeping the positions exactly (cast `notInterruptible` at 8, channel at 7). Keep the secret-safety comments: these are still never compared.
- `modules/IconGrid.lua:176-181` (`instanceCasting`) and `modules/IconGrid_Visibility.lua:197-207` (`resolveInterruptible`): the same conversion.
- `modules/Castbar.lua:758-759` (`Reevaluate`): `NS.Compat.UnitExists` and `NS.Compat.UnitIsDead`.

- Keep the `_G.` prefix rule (`tests/test_source_style.lua`) satisfied inside Compat. Behaviour while no simulation runs must be byte-for-byte identical, so every existing suite passes unedited.

- `docs/midnight-quirks.md`: one sentence. The new readers pass secrets through untouched, exactly as the inline reads did.

items.title: One dispatch table: a route registry fed by RegisterEventList and NewUnitCastFilter, and NS.DeliverEvent replaying exactly the client's handlers (simulator prerequisite, H3)
items.spec:
WHY. H3 requires one `deliver` that calls exactly the handlers the client's registration would call for any event. KickCD has no single table. Game events reach six AceEvent targets through `NS.RegisterEventList` (`core/CoreSetup.lua:85-92`), and the `UNIT_SPELLCAST_*` family reaches private per-unit filter frames built by `Util.NewUnitCastFilter` (`core/Util.lua:513-540`). Both are already single choke points, so recording there is the minimal change.

TESTS FIRST. New `tests/test_event_routes.lua`, registered in `tests/run.lua`. Write it red, then green:
1. After the full `T.load` lifecycle:
   - `NS.DeliverEvent("SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN")` runs Cooldowns' `OnCooldownEvent` exactly once and answers 1;
   - `"PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED"` runs IconGrid's `OnTargetChanged`, Castbar's `OnTargetChanged`, and UnitLabel's handler if it registers one; it answers that count, with each handler spied;
   - `"PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED"` reaches `core/State.lua`'s boot listener (`NS.State.inCombat` becomes true and `COMBAT_STATE` is sent).
2. `NS.DeliverEvent("UNIT_SPELLCAST_START", "target", guid, id)` runs IconGrid's `OnUnitCastEvent` and Castbar's `OnCastStart` for the TARGET instances only. The same call with `"focus"` reaches only the focus instances. With `"party1"` it runs nothing and answers 0.
3. A disarmed filter: disable the focus unit, then deliver `UNIT_SPELLCAST_START` for `"focus"`. Nothing runs.
4. Stood down (`NS.SetMasterEnabled(false)`): every event answers 0, because every target unregistered and every filter is disarmed. It does not depend on a latch check inside `DeliverEvent`.
5. An event nobody registered (`GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`) answers 0.
6. A handler that raises: the rest still run, the count includes it, and one `Events` debug line names the handler. Per-handler isolation is the host's (H3).
7. A registration made through `NS.SafeRegisterEvent` directly (not the list) is NOT a route. This pins the KC-06 watch target staying outside deliver.

IMPLEMENTATION.
- New `core/Events.lua`. In `KickCD.toc` it goes directly after `core\CoreSetup.lua`, with a comment: conventional position; it defines nothing other files read at load, and the recorders are called at runtime.
  - `NS.EventRoutes = { targets = {}, byTarget = {}, filters = {} }`.
  - `NS.EventRoutes.RecordList(target, list)` appends `target` to `targets` the first time it is seen, keeping registration order.
  - `NS.EventRoutes.RecordFilter(module, unit, routes, filter)` appends `{ module, unit, routes, filter }`.
  - `NS.DeliverEvent(event, ...)`:
    - for a `UNIT_SPELLCAST_` event: for each recorded filter with `filter.armed`, `unit == (...)` and `routes[event]`, pcall `module[routes[event]](module, event, ...)` and count it;
    - for every event: read `local reg = LibStub("AceEvent-3.0").events; local list = reg and type(reg.events) == "table" and reg.events[event]`; for each recorded target in order whose `list[target]` is a function, pcall `list[target](event, ...)` (CallbackHandler's stored callable, called the way its `Fire` calls it) and count it;
    - if `reg.events` is not a table, answer 0 and write `NS.Debug("Events", "deliver: AceEvent registry unreadable")` once;
    - an error writes `NS.Debug("Events", "handler for %s failed: %s", event, NS.SafeToString(err))`;
    - answer the count.
  - Keep every function CCN 15 or less: split the cast-filter walk and the AceEvent walk into two locals.
- `core/CoreSetup.lua:85` `NS.RegisterEventList`: first line `if NS.EventRoutes then NS.EventRoutes.RecordList(target, list) end`. It is resolved at call time, and CoreSetup loads before Events.lua, but this is only called at runtime.
- `core/Util.lua` `NewUnitCastFilter`: after building `filter`, `if NS.EventRoutes then NS.EventRoutes.RecordFilter(module, unit, routes, filter) end`. The filter is built once per (module, unit) and re-armed, so the record never duplicates.
- No behaviour change while no simulation runs: `DeliverEvent` has no caller until KC-05.

DOCS.
- `docs/data-flow.md`: a "Simulated delivery" subsection.
  - What `DeliverEvent` replays: still-registered AceEvent routes, in registration order, and armed cast filters for the event's unit.
  - That the client dispatches AceEvent targets in `pairs` order, and why no KickCD event depends on the order between two handlers.
  - The CallbackHandler `registry.events` read, and its debug-line fallback.
- `docs/module-map.md`: a row for `core/Events.lua`.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: *Load order* and the module-map row.

  - `newSeamStub()` and `newSimStub(say)` copied from the reference stub, with the line `NS.L["The simulator needs LibKa0s-Sim-1.0."]`;

- `core/KickCD.lua` `COMMANDS` (`:231`): add the row `{"sim", NS.L["Run a simulation of interrupts and cooldowns — try `/kcd sim`"], function(rest) NS.Sim:RunVerb(rest or "") end}` after `perf`.

items.title: modules/SimWorld.lua: the simulated world (player cooldowns, GCD, charges, target/focus enemies and their casts) and its seam providers
items.spec:
WHY. Every client read the engine makes during a session must be answered by the simulation (H1). This file owns the world model and the providers (design-kc-sim §5.1-5.2).

TESTS FIRST. New `tests/test_sim_world.lua`, using `sim_support`. With a world installed by `NS.SimWorld.Build(opts)` and the seam active (start a stub scenario through `NS.Sim`, or call the providers directly through `NS.SimSeam` while a test session is active), assert:
1. Cooldowns.
   - With no cooldown: `NS.Compat.GetSpellCooldown(57994)` answers `0, 0, false, 1, false` and `IsSpellUsable` answers `true, false`.
   - `SimWorld.StartCooldown(57994, 12)` at clock t: the answer is `t, 12, true, 1, true`, and `GetSpellCooldownDuration` answers a duration whose `GetTotalDuration` is 12.
   - After `advance(12)`, the expiry timer clears the cooldown and fires `SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` once (spy `NS.DeliverEvent`).
2. GCD.
   - `SimWorld.StartGcd(1.5)` makes an on-GCD spell (192058) answer active with duration 1.5. A spell marked `offGcd` (57994) answers ready.
   - When an on-GCD spell's own longer cooldown runs, that cooldown wins.
3. Charges. `SimWorld.SetCharges(57994, 2)` makes `GetSpellCharges` answer `2, 2, 0, 0`. `SimWorld.UseCharge(57994, 15)` answers `1, 2, t, 15`. The recharge timer fires `SPELL_UPDATE_CHARGES` and restores 2. At 0 charges, `GetSpellCooldown` answers `isActive` true.
4. Units and casts.
   - `SetUnit("target", "casterA")`: `UnitExists("target")` is true, `UnitCanAttack("target")` is true and `UnitIsDead` is false. `UnitExists("party1")` is false and `UnitExists("player")` is true.
   - `StartCast("casterA", {spellID, name, duration = 3, notInterruptible = false})`: `UnitCastingInfo("target")` answers the client's nine positions (name at 1, texture at 3, `notInterruptible` at 8, spellID at 9), and `UnitCastingDuration` answers a 3 s duration.
   - A channel answers through `UnitChannelInfo` (`notInterruptible` at 7) and nil through `UnitCastingInfo`.
   - `Compat.GetCastingInfo("target")` composes the record (no provider of its own).
   - The same enemy set as focus answers the same cast on `focus`.
5. Idle seam: with no session, every member answers the live (mocked) client.
6. No world while active (a defensive path): providers call `fallback(...)`.
7. `Compat.NewDuration` answering nil makes `SimWorld.CanBuild()` false.

IMPLEMENTATION. New `modules/SimWorld.lua` (TOC: first of the sim block, after `modules\UnitLabel.lua`). `NS.SimWorld = NS.SimWorld or {}`. The world lives on `NS.SimHost.world`.
- `Build(opts)` answers `{ units = {}, enemies = {}, spells = {}, gcd = nil, combat = false, timers = {} }`.
- Mutators, each pure world edits that fire nothing (the drivers fire):
  - `SetUnit(unit, key|nil)`, `AddEnemy(key, {name, hostile})`, `Kill(key)`;
  - `StartCast(key, cast)`, `EndCast(key)`, `SetInterruptible(key, bool)`;
  - `StartCooldown(id, dur)`, `ClearCooldown(id)`, `StartGcd(dur)`;
  - `SetCharges(id, max)`, `UseCharge(id, recharge)`, `MarkOffGcd(id)`.
- `StartCooldown` and `UseCharge` schedule their expiry with `NS.Sim:After(remaining, fn)`. Never a raw `C_Timer`: the timers die with the session. The callback clears the state and calls `NS.Sim:Fire("SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN")` (or `"SPELL_UPDATE_CHARGES"` then `"SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN"`). Keep handles in `world.timers[id]` so `ClearCooldown` (the drivers' compressed expiry) cancels them.
- The clock is `GetTime()`, read directly: it is not an answer the seam owns. The world reads nothing else from the client.
- Providers, registered ONCE at file load with `NS.SimSeam:SetProvider(key, fn(fallback, ...))`, for:
  - `GetSpellCooldown`, `GetSpellCooldownDuration`, `GetSpellCharges`, `IsSpellUsable`;
  - `UnitExists`, `UnitCanAttack`, `UnitIsDead`;
  - `UnitCastingInfo`, `UnitChannelInfo`, `UnitCastingDuration`, `UnitChannelDuration`.
- Each provider reads `NS.SimHost.world` at call time and answers `fallback(...)` when it is nil.
- The durations come from `NS.Compat.NewDuration(start, dur)`. An idle spell answers `NewDuration(0, 0)`, the client's "live but zeroed" shape (`core/Compat.lua:133-138`).
- Keep each provider small (CCN 15 or less): a `cooldownOf(id)` helper, and `castTuple(cast, isChannel)` returning the positional values.
- `SimWorld.CanBuild()` reports whether `NewDuration(GetTime(), 1)` is non-nil.
- Do not provide `GetSpellInfo`, `GetSpellTexture`, `IsSpellAvailable` or `GetSpecialization*`. They answer live: the player's real spells, design D4.

DOCS. `docs/module-map.md` row, and `docs/compat-layer.md` "which members the simulator answers" (the provider list).

items.title: Real-world interference and destructive surfaces: auto-stop on combat/loading screen/group/profile/unlock, stand-down stops first, resetall and unlock refuse, diagnostics sim section
items.spec:
WHY. #38 says the simulation stops by itself when the real world interferes. H5 refuses destructive commands. H6 makes the stand-down stop come first. H8 adds a diagnostics section (design-kc-sim D10 and §6).

TESTS FIRST. Extend `tests/test_sim_session.lua`, or add `tests/test_sim_interference.lua` if the first passes 600 lines. With a session running, assert:
1. A REAL `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED`, fired through the kit's AceEvent `__fireEvent` and not through `NS.Sim:Fire`: the session stops with the `combat` stop line, and `NS.State.inCombat` stays true afterwards (no cleanup REGEN_ENABLED).
2. A real `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` stops it with `world`.
3. A real `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` with `IsInGroup` true stops it with `group`. With `IsInGroup` false it keeps running.
4. A simulated `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` (via `NS.Sim:Fire`) never reaches the watch target.
5. A profile switch (`NS.db:SetProfile`) stops it with `profile`.
6. `Store.Set("locked", false)` (the settings checkbox path) stops it with `unlocked`.
7. `/kcd unlock`, `/kcd toggle` and `NS.ToggleLock()` (the launcher) are refused with `L["End the simulation first (/kcd sim stop)."]`, and `locked` stays true.
8. `/kcd resetall` is refused with the same line, and `KickCDDB` is unchanged.
9. `/kcd disable` stops the session FIRST, with the `standDown` line, before any module's Suspend. Spy the order: the `Sim:Stop` call precedes `IconGrid:Suspend`.
10. A real `PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED` and a real `UNIT_SPELLCAST_START` on target are absorbed: the session keeps running, and the cast bar still shows the simulated cast.
11. The watch target holds no registration while idle (`mocks.__registrationSet()` has no `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`), and `tests/test_disabled.lua` stays green unedited.
12. `/kcd diagnostics` writes a `sim` section:
    - idle: `sim: idle`;
    - running: scenario, step `pos/total`, events count, kick and cc spell ids, and simulated combat on or off.

IMPLEMENTATION.
- `modules/Sim.lua`: `Host.watch = {}`, embedded with `LibStub("AceEvent-3.0"):Embed(Host.watch)`.
  - In `Host.Prepare`, register `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED`, `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` and `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` with `NS.SafeRegisterEvent(Host.watch, ev, handler, NS.State.rejectedEvents)`. Use it directly, NOT `NS.RegisterEventList`, so the watch is never a deliver route (KC-02 pins this).
  - `OnStop` calls `Host.watch:UnregisterAllEvents()`.
  - The handler returns at once when `NS.Sim:IsDelivering()`, then maps the event to its reason. For `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE` it stops only when `NS.SimSeam:Live(function() return _G.IsInGroup and _G.IsInGroup() end)` is true.
  - Call `NS.Sim:Stop(reason)`.
- The profile stop: in `core/Database.lua:644` `Database:OnProfileChanged`, first line `if NS.Sim and NS.Sim:IsActive() then NS.Sim:Stop("profile") end`.
- The unlock stop for the settings checkbox: in `modules/IconGrid.lua` `OnConfigChanged` (`:821`), on the `general` section, `if profile.locked == false and NS.Sim and NS.Sim:IsActive() then NS.Sim:Stop("unlocked") end` before the existing branch. Keep it CCN 15 or less by putting it in a local helper.
- The CLI refusals in `core/KickCD.lua`:
  - `setLocked` (`:172`): when `value` is false and `NS.Sim:IsActive()`, `return refuse(self, "Set", verb, nil, "simulation running", NS.L["End the simulation first (/kcd sim stop)."])`. This covers `unlock`, `toggle` and `NS.ToggleLock`.
  - `runResetAll` (`:578`): the same refusal at the top.
- H6: `core/LifecycleSetup.lua:118` `standDown()`, first line `if NS.Sim and NS.Sim.IsActive and NS.Sim:IsActive() then NS.Sim:Stop("standDown") end`. This covers `disable` and the perf hold.
- H8: `modules/Diagnostics.lua`:
  - `function X.Sim(out)` reads `NS.Sim:Status()` and `NS.SimHost` (kick, cc, `Session().simCombat`), and writes one line each;
  - add `{ "sim", X.Sim }` to `X.Sections()` (`:259`) after `perf`;
  - extend `tests/test_diagnostics.lua`'s expected section list.
- Locales: every new line.

DOCS.
- `docs/slash-dispatch.md`: `resetall` and `lock`/`unlock`/`toggle` rows say they refuse while a simulation runs.
- `docs/debug.md` or the diagnostics doc: the `sim` section.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: *The disabled state*. The stand-down's first step stops a simulation.

items.title: modules/SimDrivers.lua: one state-driven driver per step kind, firing the client's events in client order
items.spec:
WHY. `play` drives one step's events through `sim:Fire`. KickCD's drivers must read the world before acting, so a paused run, a click-ahead or a slow pace never prints a false `[sim]` line (design-kc-sim §5.3).

TESTS FIRST. New `tests/test_sim_drivers.lua`, using `sim_support` and a running session (a test scenario). For each kind, spy `NS.DeliverEvent` and assert the exact event sequence, the world edit, the returned detail and the `[sim]` lines (spy `NS.Util.print`):
- `Combat {on = true}`: fires `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED`, sets `Session().simCombat = true`, and `NS.State.inCombat` becomes true. `{on = false}` fires `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`.
- `Target {enemy}` and `Focus {enemy|nil}`: set the unit and fire `PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED` / `PLAYER_FOCUS_CHANGED`.
- `CastStart {enemy, spell, duration, uninterruptible?}`: fires `UNIT_SPELLCAST_START` for every unit currently showing that enemy (target and/or focus), with `(unit, castGUID, spellID)`.
- `ChannelStart`: the same, with `UNIT_SPELLCAST_CHANNEL_START`.
- `Interruptible {enemy}`: flips the flag and fires `UNIT_SPELLCAST_INTERRUPTIBLE`.
- `Kick {enemy}` (the player's kick):
  - (a) no cast: a `[sim]` line, fires nothing, detail `no cast`;
  - (b) uninterruptible: `[sim]` "cast is uninterruptible", fires nothing;
  - (c) kick on cooldown with no charge: `[sim]` "your kick is on cooldown (Ns)", fires nothing;
  - (d) success: starts the cooldown or uses a charge, and fires `UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED` (`player`), `SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN` (plus `SPELL_UPDATE_CHARGES` for a charge spell), then `UNIT_SPELLCAST_INTERRUPTED` (or `_CHANNEL_STOP` for a channel) for each unit showing the enemy, and ends the cast.
- `PartyKick {member, enemy}`: `[sim]` "<name> (<spec>) interrupts <enemy> with <spell>", then `UNIT_SPELLCAST_INTERRUPTED`. With no cast, only narration.
- `Complete {enemy}`: fires `UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED` then `UNIT_SPELLCAST_STOP` (or `_CHANNEL_STOP`) and ends the cast.
- `Cc {enemy}`:
  - with no CC spell resolved: narration only;
  - otherwise: starts the CC cooldown (fixed 30 s) and a 1.5 s GCD, fires `UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED` (`player`) and `SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN`, and narrates.
- `Die {enemy}`: `Kill`; ends any cast with `UNIT_SPELLCAST_STOP`; clears target and focus that show it, firing their change events.
- `Leave {member}`: narration, then fires `GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE`. That answers 0 delivered and must not raise.
- `Expire {spell = "kick"|"cc"}`: compressed time. It cancels the timer, clears the cooldown or restores the charges, and fires `SPELL_UPDATE_CHARGES`/`SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN`.

The role words `"kick"` and `"cc"` resolve to `NS.SimHost.kick` and `NS.SimHost.cc` at play time. The timeline stays pure.

IMPLEMENTATION.
- New `modules/SimDrivers.lua`. TOC order:
  1. after `modules\SimWorld.lua`;
  2. before `modules\Sim.lua`.
  `NS.SimDrivers = { DRIVERS = {}, EVENTS = {} }`.
- `EVENTS[kind]`: the list of event names each kind can fire. `Sim.lua`'s `stepTip` reads it for its Fires line.
- Every driver:
  - is `function(step) ... return detail end`;
  - fires only through `NS.Sim:Fire`;
  - edits the world only through `NS.SimWorld` mutators;
  - prints narration through `Host.Say(line)`, which is `NS.Util.print(NS.L["[sim] %s"]:format(line))`.
- Spell names in narration come from `NS.Compat.GetSpellInfo(id)` (live). Enemy and member names come from the scenario's data (`step.enemy` keys resolve through `NS.SimHost.world.enemies`; members through `NS.SimScenario.PARTY`, arriving in KC-08 and read at call time).
- Durations are constants in the file:
  - `KICK_CD = 15`;
  - `CC_CD = 30`;
  - `GCD = 1.5`;
  - charge recharge 15.
- `castGUID` is a counter string, `"Cast-sim-<n>"`.
- `Kick`'s branches are a small decision function and four helpers. The CCN limit is 15 per function.
- Locales: every narration line uses a format key.

DOCS. `docs/module-map.md` row; `docs/data-flow.md` the simulated event sequences per kind (one table).

items.spec:
Branch feat/2026-10-23-sim-preview-mode-strips in ../WowAddonStandards. Follow its CLAUDE.md: US English, LF, `filename-§N` citations, and no numbered heading in the eleven unnumbered files (preview-mode, versioning-git are among them). Do NOT bump the version or date: WS-00 opened v2.87.0. Re-read each file first, because earlier WS items in this run may have edited preview-mode.md.

1. standards/standards/preview-mode.md: append at the END of the file (after the simulator section's last paragraph) a new unnumbered heading `### Kept current at every release (MUST)` with this substance, in the file's voice:
- Applies to every addon that ships a test mode, a preview drawn by unlocking, or a simulator. A frameless addon, with no positionable display and no simulator, owes only the Not applicable answer.
- At every version bump (versioning-git) the addon MUST re-look at its placeholder data and its simulator scenarios and their suites:
  (1) Coverage: every display element and feature the release adds or changes that the preview draws appears in the placeholder data, and every event-driven feature added since the previous release that a scenario could exercise is in a scenario step, or the scenario list says why it is not.
  (2) Currency: data naming game content (item, spell, encounter, instance, currency and affix ids or names, the season's dungeon list, level and item-level ranges) matches the season and patch the release targets (the TOC `## Interface:`, toc-file-§3).
  (3) Fidelity: the data and the scenarios still drive the current render path, verbs and UI, with no field the display stopped reading, no removed option, and no step driving a control that is gone.
- MUST record the outcome in that release run's ANALYSIS.md under `## Preview and simulation data` (automated-tests-§5) with exactly one answer: Current; Refreshed (citing the commits); Deferred (naming the reason; SHOULD cite a GitHub issue); or Not applicable (frameless, as above). The section lists the files reviewed. `/dev-copilot:bump-version` asks the question before its release gate and writes the section. A release recorded by hand asks the owner the same question.
- Why at release: data naming game content ages with every patch, and nothing else revisits it. The measured shape: the test-mode strip and the simulator arrived in v2.86.0, and their data and scenarios have no other checkpoint.
- Commencement: each addon's first release after v2.87.0. Release bundles frozen earlier are not backfilled (automated-tests-§5).
- Not an anti-pattern number. A missing or answerless section is a MUST finding against preview-mode.

2. standards/standards/versioning-git.md: insert after line 6 (the `dev-copilot:bump-version` bullet) a bullet: **MUST**, at every version bump, re-look at the test-mode data and simulator scenarios and record the answer in the release run's ANALYSIS.md (preview-mode, *Kept current at every release*). Name the heading in words, never §N.
